transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen, Daniel Park, Maya Singh, Leo Martinez, Sara O'Neill, Ravi Kapoor + All employees (remote)

Summary (auto): Leadership update; Q2 results, roadmap, hiring, security, Q&A.

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, uh, welcome to the July leadership update. Thanks for joining, especially those in EMEA and APAC, obviously early for some of you. We'll try to keep it crisp, we got a lot to cover. 
[00:20] Ava Chen: Quick agenda - Q2 highlights, product roadmap, hiring/org, security/compliance, then open Q&A. Daniel will go over infrastructure and the SOC2 progress, Maya will go over product, Leo will do a short customer highlights section.
[00:38] Daniel Park: thanks, Ava. Hi all - short infra update. Q2 throughput improvements are shipping - we've reduced tail latency on long sequences by about 18% on average for hosted endpoints, that's with the new kernel selection fallback and improved KV cache warm starts. Not perfect, um, some workloads still spike, but better.
[01:04] Daniel Park: We're also piloting faster autoscaling for Dedicated - this, uh, will cut cold-start penalty when capacity needs to ramp, important for customers with bursty traffic. We had one big POC last week where burst traffic came up 4x and the fallback routing worked, which is good.
[01:24] Maya Singh: Quick product notes - we pushed an early alpha for the Optimize recommendations engine; it surfaced batching + quantization suggestions for three internal workloads and the estimated unit-cost savings looked promising, around 30% in those tests. Caveat, results vary by model and prompt length.
[01:46] Maya Singh: For Private we improved the onboarding checklist - customers can now self-serve the VPC peering step for a subset of cloud providers which should shave a week off heavy customers' onboarding. Still working on the on-prem packaging docs.
[02:05] Leo Martinez: Sales highlights - closed three mid-market deals, one Named Deal conversion to Dedicated reserved capacity, and a larger enterprise pilot moved to a procurement review. We're seeing stronger interest around Private for regulated customers in finance and healthcare. Renewal conversations largely positive.
[02:28] Sara O'Neill: Hiring update - we've filled 8 roles in Q2, including two production infra hires and a senior backend for the runtime team. We still have high priority IC roles open, see the hiring doc. We're going to tighten the interview loop to reduce offer lag.
[02:46] Ava Chen: Financials - high level: ARR growth is healthy, but margins are still under pressure from bursty GPU utilization. We're holding to plan but we need to continue improving unit economics; that's on the product + infra teams to drive Optimize and routing improvements.
[03:05] Audience: applause / clapping (background)
[03:18] Ava Chen: Ok let's dig into Q&A. Please keep questions short, we'll try to get to as many as possible.

[03:30] Audience - Leonard (Engineering): Hey - quick question on the Dedicated autoscale - is the policy going to be customer-configurable or we set safe defaults?
[03:41] Daniel Park: Good question. The plan is safe defaults for 90% of customers, with advanced knobs for dedicated customers and platform teams. We'll expose policies in the console and APIs, and SEs can help tune for big pilots.
[03:59] Leonard: Cool, thanks.

[04:05] Audience - Priya (Sales): on Optimize, are the recommendations actionable via API or is it a manual playbook?
[04:14] Maya Singh: Initially it's an insights report + suggested config (batching window, quantization profile, cache TTLs). We plan an API in the next quarter to export recommended profiles directly. That's part of the roadmap items we'll publish.
[04:30] Priya: awesome.

[04:35] Audience - External sounding name (maybe wrong): Will we support HSM integrations for key management soon?
[04:41] Ravi Kapoor: Yes - KMS is supported, HSM roadmap is in progress. We're working with partners for the HSM certs and expect an initial offering for Private by Q4. Exact timeline TBD - I'll share the SOC2 and HSM timeline after this meeting.

[05:02] Audience - Marco (Customer Success): Any updates on data residency / EU region rollouts?
[05:08] Ava Chen: We're prioritizing Europe and have the EU region in beta with a small set of customers; expanding access next quarter. Data residency requirements for some customers mean Private is still the primary option.

[05:24] Audience - Hannah (Finance): runway question - are we comfortable with the current burn vs plan?
[05:30] Ava Chen: Yes, we're comfortable for now; revenue is tracking up but we need to keep an eye on gross margins. We have contingency plans if the sales cycle slips.

[05:45] Daniel Park: quick tech note - some internal names get mangled in transcripts, sorry, but the tf - the term I used was kernel selection fallback, not kernal selection fallback - apologies for the transcript stuff.

[06:00] Ava Chen: Ok a couple of product deep dives - Maya?
[06:04] Maya Singh: Sure. On the roadmap: next 90 days focus is three things: 1) Dedicated autoscaling and improved burst policies, 2) Optimize GA with report exports and API, 3) Private onboarding improvements including better documentation and an on-prem packaging option. We're also investing in eval tooling to detect quality regressions before deploys.
[06:29] Maya Singh: We also have two experimental items: cheap-embedding caching for repeated vector lookups and a new reranking pipeline optimized for low-latency search. Both are experiments, not guaranteed ship.

[06:50] Leo Martinez: From GTM - we're packaging an enterprise starter pack: Dedicated baseline + 6-month onboarding + security audit for regulated customers. Helps move pilots into committed contracts.

[07:04] Audience - Q (People Ops): Are we hiring more sales vs engineering this quarter?
[07:10] Sara O'Neill: We'll keep a balance - priority is infra and product engineers to improve unit economics, but we'll add quota-carrying sellers where we have pipeline. Headcount plan will be posted in the hiring doc.

[07:26] Audience - Sam (Support): Support SLAs question - any change to response/resolve times for Dedicated customers?
[07:33] Leo Martinez: SLA tiers will be clearer in the Console page and docs; Dedicated customers will get faster support and escalation paths, plus optional premium monitoring add-ons.

[07:50] Audience - Claire (RL): Any updates on open-source model catalog integrations?
[07:55] Maya Singh: We're adding a curated catalog of verified open models with performance profiles - helps customers pick low-latency compatible variants. It's live in alpha.

[08:10] Audience chatter / muted lines

[08:20] Ava Chen: ok, a few operational asks - one, please do the follow-up survey we'll send; two, managers please post team-level OKRs by Friday; three, leadership office hours sign-up.

[08:33] Ava Chen: we'll circle back on SOC2 timeline, Maya will publish roadmaps, Leo will circulate the renewals list, and Ravi/Sara will coordinate security and hiring follow-ups.

[08:47] Audience - Anonymous: are we doing a product town hall soon?
[08:51] Maya Singh: yes, planning a product AMA the week after next - exact invite to go out in calendar today or tomorrow.

[09:02] Ava Chen: Great - last bit, shout-outs. Big thanks to infra for the kernel work, and customer success for moving those pilots.

[09:16] Audience: applause

[09:22] Ava Chen: Ok we'll end there, recording and notes will be posted, thanks.

[09:29] End meeting notes: Total time - 65 minutes. Recording to be shared.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcribed, occasional name errors (HSM spelled H-S-M sometimes), minor punctuation issues.
